findings.finding: HCA's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-27) puts the exchange-driven uninsured payer-mix hit at ~$400M pre-tax in Q3, against ~$400M in Q2 of which ~$75M was a Q1 catch-up (so ~$325M underlying): the headwind grew roughly 20-25% q/q; HCA same-facility ER visits +5.1% (Q2 +3.6%) while surgeries stayed negative (inpatient -1.4%, outpatient -3.7%; Q2 -2.3%/-3.4%), i.e. no commercial elective recovery. CYH's guide assumed H2 ACA impact like Q2 (~$20M/quarter at midpoint) and hoped elective surgery would recover in Q3/early Q4; read across, CYH's Q3 mix is more likely at or below the Q2 run-rate than better.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints, both payer-mix/volume misses with guide cuts, traded -13.66% (2026-07-22) and -12.58% (2026-04-21) per the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: HCA printed one session before CYH; CYH is -0.9% over 5 days and has no post-HCA estimate revisions found. If the market had translated HCA's acceleration onto CYH, CYH would have sold off on 10-27/10-28 or analysts would have trimmed Q3; neither visible. Scale: CYH's own ACA hit is ~$20-25M a quarter against ~$330M of EBITDA, so the transmission is small in dollars.
findings.independence: Q2 comparison from HCA's Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000860730/000119312526315151/hca-ex99_1.htm and the $75M Q1 catch-up from https://www.hcinnovationgroup.com/finance-revenue-cycle/hospital-and-health-system-operations/news/55390982/jump-in-uninsured-patients-stings-hca (2026-07-15). CYH assumptions from its Q2 call https://www.webull.com/news/15277474514609153. Proxy: a peer, not CYH's own number.

findings.finding: UHS Q3 2026 (2026-10-27): acute same-facility adjusted admissions +4.9% (Q2 +2.9%) but net revenue per adjusted admission -1.7% (Q2 +3.0%); volume up, price/mix down, the same shape CYH reported in Q2 when about half its volume growth was uninsured with minimal revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CYH fell -13.66% on 2026-07-22 when it disclosed volume growth that was half uninsured and cut its guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Released after the close of 10-27, one session before CYH; no read-through to CYH found. UHS Q2 rev/adj admission may have carried supplemental-payment items, so part of the swing may be timing, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: UHS Q2 comparison: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000352915/000119312526318940/uhs-ex99_1.htm. Shares its cause (exchange disenrollment) with finding 1 but is a different company's document; sized down for that overlap.

findings.finding: HCA said on 2026-10-27 it now expects full-year 2026 results in the upper half of the ranges it reissued on 2026-07-14, despite the $400M Q3 payer-mix hit, so the largest peer absorbed the headwind without a further cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CYH has not had a guide maintained or raised since 2025; the +25.77% on 2025-10-23 was its last strong positive reaction (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Sector-level relief that HCA's scale and Florida supplemental payments make hard to transfer to CYH; its HCA guide excludes future state-program approvals. Small for that reason.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1 (two readings of one release: the headwind and the guide); sizes kept apart because they land on different lines.

findings.finding: CYH's own guide makes the low end of its EBITDA range the case where Florida's 2026 state-directed payments are not recognized by year-end; the latest public record found is CMS approval (April 2026) of the Florida hospital DPP for Oct 2024-Sep 2025 only, with the 2025-26 program still to be sought, so absent a new approval CYH tracks toward the lower half and may narrow the range down.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the low end of the guide already assumes no Florida 2026 payment, so this lands inside guidance. What is unpriced is only the narrowing; HCA's Q2 recognized Florida DPP revenue through 2026-06-30, which leaves open that an approval exists that CYH has not yet booked (an upside case not resolved here).
findings.independence: CYH's Q2 call states the low/high-end assumption: https://www.webull.com/news/15277474514609153; HCA Q2 Florida recognition through June 2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000860730/000119312526315151/hca-ex99_1.htm. These point in opposite directions on whether a 2025-26 approval exists, so the size is small.

findings.finding: Florida lost about 450,000 effectuated ACA enrollees in 2026 (4.3M to 3.85M, -10%), the largest absolute loss of any state; national effectuated enrollment fell 12% to 19.2M by February, expected to decline further through 2026.

findings.why_not_priced: Public since August and CYH already raised its ACA EBITDA impact estimate to $50-75M on 2026-07-23; mostly priced, filed as the broad series behind findings 1-2.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro series; CYH's state mix not quantified here.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call CYH said A/R days rose because payers are auditing claims before paying, after Q1 operating cash flow of -$297M and Q2 of +$87M; leverage was 6.7x with the next significant maturity in 2029. Management called it timing, not collection risk; Q3 cash flow is a line the print will be read on.
findings.why_not_priced: Public on the July call; no new data found on Q3 collections. Filed for the panel at zero, direction unknown.
